note: P4282 (Pro 26:17) — meddling in a quarrel not one's own is like seizing a passing dog by the ears.

dims.v: officiousness — seizing a quarrel not one's own, like grabbing a stray dog's ears
the meddling that seizes on a quarrel not one's own, as reckless as grabbing a passing dog by the ears — officiousness that invites a bite for nothing
(the quarrel not his own that he seizes)
the officious intrusion that courts needless harm

chazaq (seize/take hold) — 'whoever meddles in a quarrel not his own is like one who TAKES a passing dog by the ears' (26:17); to intrude on others' disputes is to court a bite for nothing. Officiousness invites the harm it had no need to risk.
